justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated R6 core compatibility StructureDefinition while moving active GraphDefinition work to an incubator or external package.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy validation, but keeps a low-maturity resource in core and risks duplicate core/incubator representations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The likely goal--removing or externalizing a trial-use/FMM 1 graph-definition resource from core--is reasonable, and a whole-resource removal is a coherent way to avoid continued base-maintenance obligations. The breakage is still significant for existing R4 instances, and the local evidence lacks official ballot rationale, so this is only probably justified rather than fully justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have retained `GraphDefinition` as a deprecated compatibility resource, possibly with narrative directing new implementations to the API-incubator artifact. That would preserve most R4-valid instances and generated resource-type support. The material tradeoff is that core would continue to publish and maintain an experimental same-resource representation while a successor evolves elsewhere, creating validation ambiguity and a deprecated representation that might persist indefinitely.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 local element tree only as part of a deprecated core compatibility GraphDefinition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old element paths, but only by carrying the removed experimental model and any competing replacement in parallel.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Loss of the local elements follows directly from the apparent decision to remove or externalize the resource. If that resource-level goal is accepted, dropping the recursive R4 element tree from core is probably reasonable. The evidence does not prove the replacement design or migration rationale, so the verdict remains qualified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept the R4 `GraphDefinition` element tree in R6 core as deprecated compatibility content, preserving paths such as `GraphDefinition.start`, `GraphDefinition.link.target.type`, and compartment rules. This is only a partial alternative because it depends on retaining the whole resource and could leave implementers with two same-purpose models--the legacy core tree and the external/incubator successor--with ongoing code-generation, validation, and interoperability cost.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the small graph compartment CodeSystems and ValueSets in R6 core or explicitly carry their canonicals in the replacement package.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Helps legacy converters, but leaves orphaned or duplicate terminology if GraphDefinition itself is no longer a core resource.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: If GraphDefinition was deliberately removed from core, removing its private graph-compartment terminology from core is probably reasonable because no remaining core element binds to it. The break is mostly a secondary converter/legacy-validation issue, and the absence of official migration evidence prevents a stronger verdict.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking terminology path could have retained `graph-compartment-use` and `graph-compartment-rule` in core, or ensured canonical continuity in the external replacement package. That would not by itself make R4 `GraphDefinition` instances valid in R6 core, so it is only partial. It also risks cluttering core with terminology that has no core binding and may diverge from the terminology owned by an incubator successor.
